setlist_extra.title: Candyman and The Music Never Stopped

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Fire On The Mountain** (2 reviews): The uptempo Fire was stellar, with Phil delivering strongly; Bob is very loud at the start of Fire; Jerry is less inventive than in earlier years [12][15]
- **Let The Good Times Roll** (1 review): Started out quiet until the sound crew got the volume cranking [10]
- **Sugaree** (1 review): Killer version with awesome background vocals [18]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Scarlet/Fire combination was a standout of the night [10]
- **The Wheel** (1 review): Tasty version emerging from space [18]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): Jerry played it beautifully; reviewer found the lyrics poignant, noting him light on his feet in black clothes [8]
- **The Weight** (1 review): In the encore, Vince sang the second verse and Phil sang the third [8]

## Setlist highlights

- **One More Saturday Night/Encore Break**: rare: 8 archived performances [19]

## The recordings

- **gd1992-12-05.AKG451.Darby.117622.Flac2448** (recommended): audience recording; 18 songs; 150 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd92-12-05.akg460.wiley.8757.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 18 songs; 155 min; rated 3.27/5 by 11 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the audience recording's sound not that great; Audience recording sounds full and rich, nearly like front-of-board, with all band members clearly present [7][15]
- **gd1992-12-05.schoeps.evans.gems.33827.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 17 songs; 165 min; rated 3.29/5 by 7 [4]. Said about its sound: Audience recording has great quality but is missing many tracks [17]
- **gd1992-12-05.140150.s2.sbd.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 10 songs; 93 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [5]

## Around the show

- Band walked out for the second set and went straight into Scarlet with no tuning pause; Jerry looked thin [7]
- Show came after Jerry's latest health scare; band sounded fresh and energetic after the hiatus; parking lot was muddy afterward [10]
- Reviewer stood on the left about thirty feet from Phil; quadrophonic sound with processed, redelivered voices felt strange [12]
- Outdoor venue older than modern sheds with a fairly flat lawn; crowd was in good spirits for Jerry's return after cancelled Veneta run [14]
- Sunny afternoon on the Compton Terrace hillside [15]
- First set is currently missing from this soundboard source [5]
- Compared to the audience recording, this version has less crowd ambience but more Phil presence and better instrument separation [11]
- Bobby's guitar is prominent in the mix on both nights; the 12/6 show may sound slightly better [14]
- Reviewer counts it among the better 1990s shows, with Vince at the top of his game [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1992-12-05.AKG451.Darby.117622.Flac2448**: taped by Mike Darby; transferred by Keo; source: Master Audience Recorded By Mr. Darby; AKGC451EB/CK1's (DID/DFC/Middle Of OTS/6 Feet High)> Whirlwind Phantoms>Sony TC-D5M,Tapes Set 1 Maxell MX-s,Set 2 Maxell… [1]. Also: Recorded by Darby with AKG 451 microphones and shared by him for this release [1]
- **gd92-12-05.akg460.wiley.8757.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Unknown; source: Audience Recording [2]
- **gd1992-12-05.schoeps.evans.gems.33827.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Todd Evans; transferred by **_**; source: Schoeps CMC32 Split Omnis -> Monster M1000 Jumpers -> Oade Pre -> MonsterM1000 Cable -> 7ft Stand -> Panasonic sv255 DAT Master from Todd Evans [4]
- **gd1992-12-05.140150.s2.sbd.miller.flac2496**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [5]. Also: Soundboard-sourced set made complete by combining two sets of masters [5]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Wolfgang's: [Grateful Dead Laminate from Compton Terrace, Dec 5, 1992 at Wolfgang's](https://www.wolfgangs.com/backstage-passes/grateful-dead/laminate/CTP921205.html) [20]
